findings.text: _job_log_receipt re-implements the receipt rule reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:752-755 already states inline, and the two copies disagree: promotion_gate anchors on the last line shaped like EXIT=<n> anywhere in the log, while landing_measure requires the receipt to be the file's final line (re.search(r"^EXIT=(\d+)\n?\Z", MULTILINE)) and additionally reports 3 when the receipt disagrees with the submission's return code. A log carrying trailing scheduler text after the receipt therefore reads as a verdict in the replay and as unreadable in the landing measure. The repair consolidated the submission form into the owner but left the receipt rule with two implementations, so a later change to that rule has two places to land.

no case in this file asserts positively that the submission's --wrap script runs the measure as an srun step; test_the_replay_is_submitted_as_a_batch_job_on_the_measure_partition checks only argv[:2] == ["sbatch", "--wait"], --partition and --chdir, and the in-place case asserts only the absence of srun. A change to reckon/crew/landing_measure.py:partition_submission that ran the script as the batch job's own shell command would leave every assertion here true. The clause the done_when states first is guarded only by tests/test_a_landing_measure_runs_on_its_partition.py:115, which asserts shlex.split(wrap)[0] == "srun" against the shared helper.
